stem: Which of the following is a role of 'hind milk' in the digestion of lactose in infants?

options.text: It contains fat which slows down the rate of absorption
It provides the high concentration of carbohydrates needed for energy
It contains concentrated lactase enzymes for the baby
It neutralizes the acidity caused by lactose fermentation

explanation: The high fat content of hind milk delays gastric emptying and transit, providing more time for the lactase enzyme to break down lactose.
rationale: Think about how the fat content affects the speed of the digestive process.

optionExplanations.A: The high fat content of hind milk delays gastric emptying and transit, providing more time for the lactase enzyme to break down lactose.
optionExplanations.B: It is the foremilk, not the hind milk, that is described as being particularly carbohydrate-rich.
optionExplanations.C: Lactase is produced by the baby's own small bowel; the milk provides the lactose, not the enzyme.
optionExplanations.D: The role of hind milk is physical/mechanical (slowing digestion) rather than a chemical neutralization of acid.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: It contains fat which slows down the rate of absorption
